about: Every optimization candidate tried or considered (research/notes/2026/10-18-optimization-inventory.md section 2), wins and no-wins alike: verdict per engine, mechanism (why it helps or not), Lean decls for and against, missing why-theorems, premises, v1 evidence, general lesson, next action. Produced by workflow findings-r1 (4 read-only analysts) at main 6d5bf87; claims carry CONFIRMED/INFERRED/OPEN in their text.

findings.candidate: batched (all reads, then all returned writes, one pass per frame)
findings.visual: open. E holds if no moved write changes a value that a later read in the same frame sees (premise NI, INFERRED true for the pilot: the hero writes --exit-opacity and pointer-events on .hero; the nav reads its own rect, the sticky profile and the track rect). Not E if batching also folds the hero-exit rAF trampoline, because the writes then land one frame earlier (v1 scroll-engine/01 note).
findings.mechanism: Style stage only. Total style passes per frame = [d ∧ (head is a read ∨ no write)] + #write-runs (PROVED: Fw.Parts.EngineScroll.total_style_closed). The engine merges only the hero's returned write run. The nav probe's two internal write→read pairs remain, so the pilot keeps 3 passes (1 with elements-skip): the moved pass comes back as the frame-end lifecycle update. Restyled elements are unchanged (same dirty sets, R2). Counter: trace.UpdateLayoutTree (det). A local run gave W equal, S equal (packages/measure-chromium/README.md:185). Core.frameWork counts [style touched] + forced, so it over-counts by 1 whenever the frame ends clean (last style access a read): PROVED Fw.Engine.frameWork_overcount; the faithful count forced + [endDirty] is Fw.Engine.frameWorkE (CONFIRMED: Chromium document.cc:2757-2762@f842f52 returns early when no style is dirty; WebKit Document.cpp:3042-3043@862f17d). Abstract closed form PROVED as Fw.Engine.flagTotal_closed: total = [d and first non-neutral access is not a write] + #write-runs (the form [d and head = R] alone fails at d, as = []). Golden finding: the forcedCountsBatched rows of Fw.Parts.Golden (engineSpecLines) are forced-only; read as totals they under-count every batched sequence that ends in a write by 1. Style totals faithful vs batched (d=true / d=false): pilot 4/3 vs 2/1 (forced alone says 1/0, so the batching saving is over-predicted by 1: 2, not 3), nav 3/2 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0), [wS,rL] 1/1 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0: batching is worse by 1 at d, not equal), [rL,wL,rL] 2/1 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0: no saving, not 1). Layout totals for the same rows move the same way for [rL,wL,rL] (2/1 vs 2/1). No golden row was edited (the rows are labelled forced counts); the Parts proofs that should move to frameWorkE are listed in docs/team/handoffs/why-core-lessons.md. Under the frame-end pass (frameWorkE) batching can also add a pass: it is worse exactly when the frame starts dirty and its first flag access is a write followed by a read (total_batch_worse_iff). The golden forcedCountsBatched rows are forced passes only: read as totals the pilot batched style row is 2/1 (dirty/clean start), not 1/0, against 4/3 faithful (Fw.Parts.Golden.pilot_batched_rows_forced_only).

findings.candidate: observers (KD#1): replace per-frame rect reads with IntersectionObserver/ResizeObserver
findings.visual: not-equal per frame. Blink delivers IO by posted task (one frame late). IO thresholds are discrete, so continuous outputs (exit opacity, morph) cannot come from IO. An IO-based hit test ignores stacking and occlusion. E only at settled states, and for boolean thresholds through a sentinel (HeroExitOpt.sentinel_iff_pointerOff) up to that lag.
findings.mechanism: It would save forced style/layout on main. Removing one reader removes a pass only if no later reader in the frame pays the same flush. The nav's elementFromPoint and rect reads stay every frame, and WebKit's scrollY forces layout (LocalDOMWindow.cpp:1466-1479@862f17d). New cost: IO compute in every lifecycle (Blink local_frame_view.cc:1148-1189; WebKit Page.cpp:2367). Blink posts delivery (intersection_observer_controller.cc:90-105). WebKit calls back inside the update, then lays out again (Page.cpp:2337, 2399). Counters: trace.IntersectionObserverCompute (det), WebKit ObserverCallback. Removing one checking read saves a pass only when the flag is dirty at the read and the next flag access after it is a write (PROVED: Fw.Parts.EngineScroll.total_remove_read).

missingWhy.statement: Observer timing: let $w$ be a write computed by an observer callback from the layout of frame $k$. Blink: $w$ is first visible in frame $k+1$. WebKit: $w$ is visible in frame $k$, and the update pays one extra style/layout pass when $w$ dirties them. Hence on crossing frames $\mathrm{obs}_v(k) = \mathrm{obs}_o(k-1)$ in Blink, and $\mathrm{passes}_v(k) = \mathrm{passes}_o(k) - \mathrm{forced}_{\mathrm{removed}} + [\mathrm{crossing}(k)]$ in WebKit.
missingWhy.needs: a per-frame step order (rAF → layout → observation → final layout) and a delivery mode per engine

missingWhy.statement: Observer dominance condition: $W_{\mathrm{obs}} \preceq W_o$ on frame $k$ iff no remaining reader in the frame checks the flag the removed read checked, and $\mathrm{crossing}(k) = 0$. Over a run, a strict gain needs $\#\{k : \mathrm{crossing}(k)\} < \#\{k : \text{read removed}\}$.
missingWhy.needs: the reader-removal lemma, the observer step above, and an IO compute unit in Stage (props or a new observe stage)

So elements-skip strictly dominates on passes but is $\preceq$ only if hit-test units are excluded from the vector.

findings.candidate: hero-exit-threaded (v6, KD#2): JS --exit-opacity writer → per-consumer CSS scroll-driven animations, plus an IO sentinel for pointer-events
findings.visual: E-s at the computed-value level under RG11 (consumer_eq_s; exact at integer scroll offsets, otherwise within the progress quantum: 1/(16R) in Chromium, 1 px on WebKit's main thread). Pixels: WebKit E in the v1 Simulator except a 30 px top band (78 levels). Chromium not-equal under the pixel rule (v1: ≤ 6 levels on 15-42k px, 1 device-px copy shift from GPU blending and snapping), so Q at best: PathPremises.raster_path fails there (INFERRED).
findings.mechanism: Removes the rAF script (FireAnimationFrame/FunctionCall −1 per scrolled frame, det), the forced track-rect read, and the inherited --exit-opacity restyle of about 230 descendants (style units, R2). Chromium: opacity and transform go to the compositor; blur stays on main (bit 12, compositor_animations.cc:405-417), so paint and raster remain. In the lane every BeginFrame keeps a style pass, so the UpdateLayoutTree count does not drop, and elementCount is quarantined (C-3). WebKit: all animations threaded (wk_all_comp), web-process work drops, the UI process and the layer count grow. PROVED (toy rasters): raster_path fails for a half-pixel translate (snap 0 vs resample 128, Fw.Engine.raster_path_fails_fracXf) and for group opacity 1/2 over child 3/10 (38 vs 39, Fw.Engine.raster_path_fails_fracAlpha), so PathPremises needs C5 and C4 (Fw.Engine.PathPremises5, shown_eq5). A compositor move adds the comp stage, so it is never framewise <= (Fw.Engine.comp_move_not_le): mixed or noClaim when the original pays no comp, trade only when it already does. Under frameWorkE both trades stand (cr_real_tradeE, wk_tradeE). Given the premise that each animated consumer adds a composited layer, the claim cannot be dominates on either engine, WebKit included (Fw.Engine.claim_ne_dominates_of_layers): at best trade.

missingWhy.statement: The lane cannot see the style saving: in lane mode $V.\mathrm{passes}(\mathrm{style}) = O.\mathrm{passes}(\mathrm{style})$ while $V.\mathrm{units}(\mathrm{style}) = N_{\mathrm{anim}} < 1 + |\mathrm{inh}(.\mathrm{hero})| = O.\mathrm{units}(\mathrm{style})$. The only count that maps to units is elementCount, which is quarantined, so `noMoreWork` cannot confirm it (`quarantined_unsound`).
missingWhy.needs: R2 inherited fan-out units in crOrig (it currently counts one change per consumer, which undercounts the original)

missingWhy.statement: Edge-frame cost on WebKit: the frames where the filter goes $\mathrm{none} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{blur}(\epsilon)$ or opacity crosses 1 pay layout: $\mathrm{layout} \in \mathrm{stages}_{wk}$ on those frames, $\#\mathrm{edgeFrames}_v \ge 1$ per rest→live switch
missingWhy.needs: tabling WebKit.opacityCross1_layout and a filter-presence clause for the variant's start and park frames

findings.candidate: strip (cd-strip, KD#12): 10 will-change faces per digit -> one 12-entry strip
findings.visual: E inside the clip window, every env/width/instant (strip_visSame from strip_shows_same); no premise beyond the restated geometry
findings.mechanism: Saving is resident: one will-change layer per face (compositing_reason_finder.cc:76-137@f842f52) becomes one per digit, 80->8 (hero_layers). Per frame, stage passes are equal (strip_passes_eq); only units drop from 10r to r (strip_units), and units are visible only in the quarantined UpdateLayoutTree.elementCount (C-3). CI can see census.layers (<o) and nothing per frame. New cost: 12 instead of 10 cells backed per digit (strip_backing_gt, full-layer rule INFERRED), so the label is trade. findings.candidate: cd-roll-ca: spring roll replaced by a WAAPI transform animation with sampled keyframes
findings.visual: E-s only at one fixed cadence, given that frame times equal the keyframe sample times (R5 clock premise). Not E across cadences: the spring integrates in min(left,16) ms slices (springLoop), so its path depends on how time is split into frames.
findings.mechanism: The roll moves from a per-frame rAF transform write (Chromium `direct`: script, style, props, commit) to a compositor transform animation (transformAnim_comp). On WebKit the legacy CA path accepts keyword-linear keyframes; legacy_rejects covers only linear() with points and steps(). Chromium saves script (FireAnimationFrame, FunctionCall: det) and the commit (cc.Commit: det) on every roll frame; lane style stays 1 per BeginFrame (F1). Each roll adds one start (style, props, commit). WebKit's web process does 0 work per frame only while nothing else renders: every rendering update ticks and invalidates every relevant animation (AnimationTimelinesController.cpp:149-177, KeyframeEffect.cpp:2129-2131@862f17d). CA asks for 80-120 Hz (PlatformCAAnimationRemote.mm:611-612), a UI-process cost no counter sees. The spring path depends on the frame split (two 8 ms steps differ from one 16 ms step, spring_split_differs), so no fixed WAAPI curve is E across cadences: E-s at one cadence only.

findings.mechanism: The original flips an attribute that a descendant rule matches, so every element of the section restyles. In WebKit the restyle also crosses #platform's size containers, adding interleaved layouts (StyleTreeResolver.cpp:1460-1480@862f17d; v1 29-32 ms style record). Per-element WAAPI pause touches only the n animated elements. The saving lands in toggle frames and in style element counts: passes stay equal, and UpdateLayoutTree.elementCount is quarantined (C-3), so CI pass counters cannot see it.
